ai.description: *Wallophis brachyura* is a slender snake reaching 40–60 cm. It is olive-brown or grey with a pale belly and lacks keeled scales. A distinctive dark streak extends from the eye to the mouth.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Indian Smooth Snake is best identified by the lack of a distinct neck and its smooth, glossy scales, which lack the prominent keels found on most other Indian colubrids.
ai.habitat: The Indian Smooth Snake inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically found in rocky, hilly terrain at elevations ranging from 300 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian smooth snake is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt small lizards and rodents within its rocky or scrubland habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Wallophis brachyura* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, though specific clutch size data remains limited.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Wallophis brachyura* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily found in the dry, arid regions of Gujarat, Rajasthan, and parts of Maharashtra.
